title: Whitehall 1212
paragraphs: A Scotland Yard crime drama built from cases in the Black Museum files, emphasizing the police investigation and evidence that lead from the discovery of a crime to its solution.

NBC police-procedural true-crime anthology based on Scotland Yard case files and Black Museum evidence. The GRH container holds one audition, 43 surviving regular broadcasts, and two OTRR reference tracks; regular episode #2 is missing from circulation.
GRH documents the program through NBC regular run (November 18, 1951 to September 28, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Percy Hoskins (performer on 43 recordings and researcher on 40 recordings), Wyllis Cooper (director on 43 recordings and writer on 43 recordings), Harvey Hayes (performer on 26 recordings), Lester Fletcher (performer on 26 recordings), Horace Braham (performer on 20 recordings), Lionel Ricou (announcer on 16 recordings), and Guy Spaull (performer on 12 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include historical true crime case, police investigation and Scotland Yard procedure, Black Museum evidence object, forensic and physical evidence, murder and homicide, and burglary, theft and property crime.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Scotland Yard Black Museum as evidentiary frame, NBC true-crime drama with an all-British cast, Whitehall 1212 and The Black Museum overlap, and Police-procedural viewpoint in early-1950s radio.
